claims.text: Elevated-temperature stress–strain, thermal-expansion, and elastic behavior in HfNbTaTiZr can be explained by gradients in grain-boundary segregation and dislocation density.
The initial material is polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial material has varying grain sizes.
The initial material has spatially varying distributions of its constituent elements.
In situ neutron diffraction and transmission electron microscopy will be used under controlled temperature and loading conditions.
Tests will cover temperatures up to 1000°C.
Tests will cover strain rates up to 10^-3 s^-1.
Grain-boundary segregation is a structural mediator of the measured responses.
Dislocation density is a structural mediator of the measured responses.
Thermally activated segregation and dislocation motion change the alloy's mechanical and thermal properties.
Yield strength will increase by 20% relative to the room-temperature baseline.
The thermal-expansion coefficient will decrease by 15% relative to the room-temperature baseline.
The hypothesis is intended to hold from 25°C to 1000°C and from 10^-5 s^-1 to 10^-3 s^-1.
The relationship among grain-boundary segregation, dislocation density, and mechanical and thermal properties may depend on grain-size distribution and impurities.
Failure to obtain at least a 15% yield-strength increase and at least a 10% thermal-expansion-coefficient decrease constitutes falsification.

contradictions.description: The predicted changes are a 20% yield-strength increase and a 15% thermal-expansion decrease, whereas falsification uses weaker thresholds of 15% and 10%. Results between these values would fail the stated prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis.
